question: In a sanitary sewer collection system, what does the acronym CMOM stand for?
correctAnswer: Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
explanation: CMOM stands for Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance. It is the US EPA framework for managing collection systems to reduce overflows.
options: Collection Monitoring and Overflow Measurement
Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
Central Maintenance Operations Manual
Capacity Measurement and Outflow Modelling
optionA: Collection Monitoring and Overflow Measurement
optionB: Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
optionC: Central Maintenance Operations Manual
optionD: Capacity Measurement and Outflow Modelling
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: What is the primary purpose of a CMOM program for a wastewater collection utility?
correctAnswer: To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
explanation: A CMOM program uses planned capacity assurance, management, operations and maintenance to prevent and reduce sanitary sewer overflows.
options: To eliminate the need for sewer cleaning
To replace all gravity sewers with force mains
To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
To transfer overflow response to property owners
optionA: To eliminate the need for sewer cleaning
optionB: To replace all gravity sewers with force mains
optionC: To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
optionD: To transfer overflow response to property owners
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: Which of the following is a core element of a documented CMOM program?
correctAnswer: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
explanation: CMOM relies on documented, scheduled operations and maintenance activities, with records that let the utility track performance and improve the program.
options: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
Responding only after a failure has been reported
Keeping no written records of overflows
Inspecting each sewer only once in its service life
optionA: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
optionB: Responding only after a failure has been reported
optionC: Keeping no written records of overflows
optionD: Inspecting each sewer only once in its service life
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: Why does a CMOM program require the utility to record the cause and location of every sanitary sewer overflow?
correctAnswer: To identify recurring problem areas so corrective work can be prioritized
explanation: Overflow records show where and why overflows repeat. That pattern is used to prioritize cleaning, repair and capacity work where it will prevent the most overflows.
options: To assign blame to individual crew members
To meet a marketing requirement for the utility
To sell the data to neighbouring utilities
To identify recurring problem areas so corrective work can be prioritized
optionA: To assign blame to individual crew members
optionB: To meet a marketing requirement for the utility
optionC: To sell the data to neighbouring utilities
optionD: To identify recurring problem areas so corrective work can be prioritized
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: Under the capacity assurance part of CMOM, what should a utility do before approving a large new development that adds flow to a trunk sewer?
correctAnswer: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
explanation: Capacity assurance means evaluating system capacity before new flows are added, so growth does not create surcharging and overflows.
options: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
Assume the trunk sewer will handle any added flow
Require the developer to operate the trunk sewer
Stop all cleaning on the trunk sewer for one year
optionA: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
optionB: Assume the trunk sewer will handle any added flow
optionC: Require the developer to operate the trunk sewer
optionD: Stop all cleaning on the trunk sewer for one year
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: What is the main purpose of a sewer condition assessment program?
correctAnswer: To prioritize repair and rehabilitation using the actual condition and risk of each asset
explanation: Condition assessment collects inspection data on each asset so repair and rehabilitation can be prioritized by condition and risk, not by age alone.
options: To repaint all manholes on a fixed colour schedule
To remove the need for flow monitoring
To increase the design flow in every sewer
To prioritize repair and rehabilitation using the actual condition and risk of each asset
optionA: To repaint all manholes on a fixed colour schedule
optionB: To remove the need for flow monitoring
optionC: To increase the design flow in every sewer
optionD: To prioritize repair and rehabilitation using the actual condition and risk of each asset
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: Which tool is most commonly used to inspect the inside of a gravity sanitary sewer?
correctAnswer: A closed circuit television camera crawler
explanation: CCTV inspection with a crawler camera is the standard method for viewing and recording the internal condition of gravity sewers.
options: A closed circuit television camera crawler
A ground penetrating radar unit only
A chlorine residual test kit
A sludge judge sampler
optionA: A closed circuit television camera crawler
optionB: A ground penetrating radar unit only
optionC: A chlorine residual test kit
optionD: A sludge judge sampler
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: For condition data to be comparable between inspections and crews, assessments should be based on what?
correctAnswer: A structured inspection method with consistent defect coding
explanation: Structured inspection with consistent defect coding makes results comparable over time and between crews, which is what allows condition trends and priorities to be set.
options: The personal opinion of each operator, recorded in free text
A structured inspection method with consistent defect coding
The age of the pipe alone
The number of complaints received that month
optionA: The personal opinion of each operator, recorded in free text
optionB: A structured inspection method with consistent defect coding
optionC: The age of the pipe alone
optionD: The number of complaints received that month
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: In asset management for sewers, how is risk usually described?
correctAnswer: Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
explanation: Risk combines how likely an asset is to fail with how serious the failure would be. A poor condition sewer under a hospital or river crossing carries higher risk than the same sewer in an open field.
options: Pipe diameter multiplied by pipe length
Age of the pipe divided by its slope
Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
Number of manholes multiplied by depth
optionA: Pipe diameter multiplied by pipe length
optionB: Age of the pipe divided by its slope
optionC: Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
optionD: Number of manholes multiplied by depth
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: Why do utilities re-inspect sewers on a planned cycle instead of inspecting each sewer only once?
correctAnswer: To track how defects change over time and update rehabilitation priorities
explanation: Repeat inspections show the rate of deterioration. That trend information updates condition grades and keeps rehabilitation priorities current.
options: To use up the inspection budget each year
To train new staff on the camera equipment
To keep the camera contractor continuously employed
To track how defects change over time and update rehabilitation priorities
optionA: To use up the inspection budget each year
optionB: To train new staff on the camera equipment
optionC: To keep the camera contractor continuously employed
optionD: To track how defects change over time and update rehabilitation priorities
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: During CCTV coding, a structural defect is graded 5 on a 1 to 5 scale. What does that grade normally mean?
correctAnswer: The pipe has failed or is likely to fail soon and needs prompt action
explanation: On a 1 to 5 structural grading scale, grade 5 is the most severe category. It indicates failure or near failure, so prompt repair or rehabilitation planning is required.
options: The pipe has a minor cosmetic blemish only
The pipe is in like new condition
The pipe has failed or is likely to fail soon and needs prompt action
The defect is an operations issue with no structural effect
optionA: The pipe has a minor cosmetic blemish only
optionB: The pipe is in like new condition
optionC: The pipe has failed or is likely to fail soon and needs prompt action
optionD: The defect is an operations issue with no structural effect
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: On a CCTV inspection, the operator sees a steady stream of clear water flowing into the sewer through a defective joint during dry weather. How should this be interpreted?
correctAnswer: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
explanation: Clear water entering through a joint or defect in dry weather is groundwater infiltration. A steady stream is recorded as a runner type infiltration observation.
options: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
As a root mass growing through the joint
As encrustation building up on the pipe wall
As a displaced joint with no water entry
optionA: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
optionB: As a root mass growing through the joint
optionC: As encrustation building up on the pipe wall
optionD: As a displaced joint with no water entry
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: Which of the following CCTV observations is a structural defect rather than an operations and maintenance defect?
correctAnswer: A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
explanation: A longitudinal crack affects the pipe structure itself, so it is a structural defect. Grease, roots and settled debris affect operation and are maintenance defects.
options: Grease deposits on the pipe wall
A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
Fine roots entering at a joint
Grit and debris settled in the invert
optionA: Grease deposits on the pipe wall
optionB: A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
optionC: Fine roots entering at a joint
optionD: Grit and debris settled in the invert
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: A CCTV report codes heavy roots at several joints in a clay sewer, with no cracks or deformation noted. What is the most appropriate first response?
correctAnswer: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
explanation: Roots are a maintenance defect. Cutting removes the blockage risk, and rapid regrowth points to treatment or joint repair rather than full replacement when the pipe is otherwise sound.
options: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
Immediately excavate and replace the entire sewer
Ignore the roots because they cause no operational effect
Line the sewer the same day without any cleaning
optionA: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
optionB: Immediately excavate and replace the entire sewer
optionC: Ignore the roots because they cause no operational effect
optionD: Line the sewer the same day without any cleaning
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: A CCTV survey has to be abandoned partway because flow depth submerges the camera. What is the correct operator action?
correctAnswer: Record the survey as abandoned, note the reason, and arrange flow control or cleaning before a repeat survey
explanation: An abandoned survey must be documented with its reason. The uninspected length has no condition data, so flow control or cleaning and a repeat survey are needed to complete the assessment.
options: Code the uninspected length as being in good condition
Delete the survey and report the sewer as fully inspected
Record the survey as abandoned, note the reason, and arrange flow control or cleaning before a repeat survey
Grade all remaining defects as grade 5
optionA: Code the uninspected length as being in good condition
optionB: Delete the survey and report the sewer as fully inspected
optionC: Record the survey as abandoned, note the reason, and arrange flow control or cleaning before a repeat survey
optionD: Grade all remaining defects as grade 5
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: What does a structured manhole assessment normally evaluate?
correctAnswer: The frame and cover, chimney, cone, wall, bench, channel and steps, plus evidence of inflow and infiltration
explanation: Manhole assessment covers each component from cover to channel, and records defects and I and I evidence so rehabilitation can be scoped component by component.
options: Only the colour of the cover
The frame and cover, chimney, cone, wall, bench, channel and steps, plus evidence of inflow and infiltration
Only the depth from rim to invert
Only whether the cover can be lifted by one person
optionA: Only the colour of the cover
optionB: The frame and cover, chimney, cone, wall, bench, channel and steps, plus evidence of inflow and infiltration
optionC: Only the depth from rim to invert
optionD: Only whether the cover can be lifted by one person
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: Inside a manhole, the concrete crown and upper wall are soft, rough and losing material, while the bench below the flow line is sound. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide released from sewage is converted to acid on moist surfaces above the flow line. That acid attacks concrete at the crown and upper wall, while submerged surfaces are largely protected.
options: Abrasion from grit in the flow
Freezing of ponded water on the bench
Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
Damage from the cover being dropped
optionA: Abrasion from grit in the flow
optionB: Freezing of ponded water on the bench
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
optionD: Damage from the cover being dropped
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: What is the purpose of a chimney seal in a manhole?
correctAnswer: To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow
explanation: The chimney area between the frame and the cone is a common inflow path during wet weather. A chimney seal blocks that path and reduces rainfall dependent inflow.
options: To support traffic loads on the frame
To make the cover easier to remove
To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow
To anchor the manhole steps to the wall
optionA: To support traffic loads on the frame
optionB: To make the cover easier to remove
optionC: To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow
optionD: To anchor the manhole steps to the wall
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: A manhole bench is broken and the channel is rough and misaligned. What operational problem is most likely to develop?
correctAnswer: Turbulence and debris accumulation that promote blockages and odours
explanation: A damaged bench and channel disrupt smooth flow through the manhole. The resulting turbulence drops solids, which build up, cause odours and can lead to blockages.
options: Turbulence and debris accumulation that promote blockages and odours
Higher pressure in the upstream force main
Lower groundwater levels around the manhole
Faster flow that cleans the upstream sewer
optionA: Turbulence and debris accumulation that promote blockages and odours
optionB: Higher pressure in the upstream force main
optionC: Lower groundwater levels around the manhole
optionD: Faster flow that cleans the upstream sewer
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: During assessment, a manhole cover is found rocking in its frame with gaps visible at the rim during rain. Why is this defect a priority?
correctAnswer: It allows surface inflow and creates a traffic and safety hazard
explanation: A rocking, poorly seated cover lets surface water pour into the manhole during rain and is a hazard to traffic and pedestrians, so it ranks as a priority repair.
options: It changes the colour of runoff entering the sewer
It prevents hydrogen sulfide from escaping, which is harmful
It increases the structural strength of the chimney
It allows surface inflow and creates a traffic and safety hazard
optionA: It changes the colour of runoff entering the sewer
optionB: It prevents hydrogen sulfide from escaping, which is harmful
optionC: It increases the structural strength of the chimney
optionD: It allows surface inflow and creates a traffic and safety hazard
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: What is a cured in place pipe (CIPP) liner?
correctAnswer: A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
explanation: CIPP uses a flexible, resin saturated tube that is inverted or pulled into the host pipe and then cured in place, forming a continuous new pipe within the old one.
options: A new rigid pipe pushed through the host pipe one joint at a time
A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
A cement mortar sprayed onto the host pipe wall
A wrap applied to the outside of an excavated pipe
optionA: A new rigid pipe pushed through the host pipe one joint at a time
optionB: A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
optionC: A cement mortar sprayed onto the host pipe wall
optionD: A wrap applied to the outside of an excavated pipe
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: Before a CIPP liner is installed, what preparation of the host pipe is required?
correctAnswer: The host pipe is cleaned and inspected by CCTV so obstructions, dimensions and lateral locations are confirmed
explanation: Cleaning and a pre-lining CCTV inspection confirm the pipe is clear, correctly sized and mapped for laterals, which prevents a failed installation and blocked connections.
options: The host pipe is cleaned and inspected by CCTV so obstructions, dimensions and lateral locations are confirmed
The host pipe is pressurized to twice its normal flow
The host pipe is filled with grout along its full length
No preparation is needed because the liner fills every defect
optionA: The host pipe is cleaned and inspected by CCTV so obstructions, dimensions and lateral locations are confirmed
optionB: The host pipe is pressurized to twice its normal flow
optionC: The host pipe is filled with grout along its full length
optionD: No preparation is needed because the liner fills every defect
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: Which methods are commonly used to cure a CIPP liner?
correctAnswer: Hot water, steam or ultraviolet light
explanation: CIPP resin is cured with heat from hot water or steam, or with ultraviolet light for UV cured systems. The cure schedule is controlled so the liner reaches its design strength.
options: Freezing, thawing and compaction
Hot water, steam or ultraviolet light
Chlorination and dechlorination
Sand blasting and painting
optionA: Freezing, thawing and compaction
optionB: Hot water, steam or ultraviolet light
optionC: Chlorination and dechlorination
optionD: Sand blasting and painting
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: Why is bypass pumping normally set up during a CIPP installation on a live sewer?
correctAnswer: To keep sewage flowing for customers while the host pipe is taken out of service and kept controlled for lining
explanation: Lining requires the host pipe to be out of normal service. Bypass pumping carries the sewage around the work section so customers stay in service and the installation stays controlled.
options: To increase flow speed so the liner installs faster
To keep sewage flowing for customers while the host pipe is taken out of service and kept controlled for lining
To test the capacity of the downstream treatment plant
To wash resin out of the liner before curing
optionA: To increase flow speed so the liner installs faster
optionB: To keep sewage flowing for customers while the host pipe is taken out of service and kept controlled for lining
optionC: To test the capacity of the downstream treatment plant
optionD: To wash resin out of the liner before curing
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: What is the main advantage of CIPP rehabilitation compared with open cut replacement?
correctAnswer: It renews the pipe structurally with little or no excavation and less surface disruption
explanation: CIPP is a trenchless method. It restores structural condition from inside the existing pipe, avoiding most excavation, restoration and traffic disruption.
options: It always costs less per metre on every project
It removes the need for any inspection before or after
It increases the pipe diameter substantially
It renews the pipe structurally with little or no excavation and less surface disruption
optionA: It always costs less per metre on every project
optionB: It removes the need for any inspection before or after
optionC: It increases the pipe diameter substantially
optionD: It renews the pipe structurally with little or no excavation and less surface disruption
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: How does pipe bursting replace an existing sewer?
correctAnswer: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
explanation: Pipe bursting pulls a bursting head through the host pipe, fracturing it outward into the soil while the new pipe is drawn in behind the head on the same alignment.
options: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
A liner is inflated inside the host pipe and left soft
The host pipe is dissolved with chemicals and flushed away
A new pipe is tunnelled parallel to the host pipe and the host is abandoned
optionA: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
optionB: A liner is inflated inside the host pipe and left soft
optionC: The host pipe is dissolved with chemicals and flushed away
optionD: A new pipe is tunnelled parallel to the host pipe and the host is abandoned
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: How does slip lining rehabilitate a sewer?
correctAnswer: By inserting a smaller new pipe into the host pipe and grouting the annular space between them
explanation: Slip lining slides a new, smaller pipe into the existing pipe and grouts the ring shaped space between them, producing a continuous new pipe inside the host.
options: By spraying a thin coating that adds no structural strength
By inserting a smaller new pipe into the host pipe and grouting the annular space between them
By bursting the host pipe and upsizing the diameter
By wrapping the outside of the pipe with steel bands
optionA: By spraying a thin coating that adds no structural strength
optionB: By inserting a smaller new pipe into the host pipe and grouting the annular space between them
optionC: By bursting the host pipe and upsizing the diameter
optionD: By wrapping the outside of the pipe with steel bands
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: What is the main hydraulic limitation of slip lining?
correctAnswer: The inserted pipe reduces the internal diameter, which can reduce capacity
explanation: Because the new pipe sits inside the host, the internal diameter gets smaller. Even with a smoother surface, the design must confirm the reduced section still carries the required flow.
options: It makes the pipe too smooth for sewage to flow
The inserted pipe reduces the internal diameter, which can reduce capacity
It requires the sewer to flow under pressure at all times
It raises the invert so much that laterals cannot connect
optionA: It makes the pipe too smooth for sewage to flow
optionB: The inserted pipe reduces the internal diameter, which can reduce capacity
optionC: It requires the sewer to flow under pressure at all times
optionD: It raises the invert so much that laterals cannot connect
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: Before pipe bursting near other buried utilities, what is the key risk that must be managed?
correctAnswer: Ground movement from bursting can damage nearby shallow utilities and services
explanation: Bursting displaces soil outward as the host pipe fractures. Nearby shallow utilities and services can be heaved or damaged, so their locations must be confirmed and monitored.
options: Ground movement from bursting can damage nearby shallow utilities and services
The new pipe will float out of the trench during installation
Resin fumes will collect in the bursting pit
The bursting head will melt plastic service lines
optionA: Ground movement from bursting can damage nearby shallow utilities and services
optionB: The new pipe will float out of the trench during installation
optionC: Resin fumes will collect in the bursting pit
optionD: The bursting head will melt plastic service lines
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: In slip lining, why is the annular space between the new pipe and the host pipe grouted?
correctAnswer: To fill the void, support the liner and prevent groundwater from migrating along the outside of the new pipe
explanation: Grouting fills the void between the pipes. It supports the inserted pipe and blocks groundwater from travelling along the annulus and entering at joints or connections.
options: To make the new pipe easier to remove later
To colour the pipe for future CCTV inspections
To fill the void, support the liner and prevent groundwater from migrating along the outside of the new pipe
To increase the flow velocity inside the new pipe
optionA: To make the new pipe easier to remove later
optionB: To colour the pipe for future CCTV inspections
optionC: To fill the void, support the liner and prevent groundwater from migrating along the outside of the new pipe
optionD: To increase the flow velocity inside the new pipe
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.

question: A utility installs temporary flow monitors at the outlets of several sub basins for an I and I study. What is the analytical value of that layout?
correctAnswer: It lets each sub basin contribution be isolated and compared, so the worst basins can be prioritized for source detection
explanation: Monitors at sub basin outlets separate the flow from each area. Comparing the responses basin by basin shows where investigation money will find the most I and I.
options: It lets each sub basin contribution be isolated and compared, so the worst basins can be prioritized for source detection
It guarantees that total plant flow will decrease during the study
It removes the need for rainfall data during the study
It measures the structural grade of every pipe in each basin
optionA: It lets each sub basin contribution be isolated and compared, so the worst basins can be prioritized for source detection
optionB: It guarantees that total plant flow will decrease during the study
optionC: It removes the need for rainfall data during the study
optionD: It measures the structural grade of every pipe in each basin
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: A depth and velocity scattergraph from a flow monitor forms a loop that rises well above the normal curve during storms. What does that pattern most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: The site is surcharging, so depth rises without a matching increase in velocity
explanation: In surcharge, depth increases under backwater conditions while velocity does not rise in proportion. The loop above the normal depth velocity relationship is a classic surcharge signature.
options: The sewer is flowing partly full and free at all times
The velocity sensor has been installed upside down
The site is surcharging, so depth rises without a matching increase in velocity
The basin has no rainfall dependent I and I
optionA: The sewer is flowing partly full and free at all times
optionB: The velocity sensor has been installed upside down
optionC: The site is surcharging, so depth rises without a matching increase in velocity
optionD: The basin has no rainfall dependent I and I
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: Why is the minimum night flow period, typically in the early morning hours, used to estimate groundwater infiltration?
correctAnswer: Legitimate sanitary use is at its lowest then, so most of the remaining flow is infiltration
explanation: In the early morning, water use by residents is minimal. Flow that remains in the sewer at that time is largely groundwater infiltration, which makes night flow a practical infiltration estimate.
options: Legitimate sanitary use is at its lowest then, so most of the remaining flow is infiltration
Rainfall never occurs during those hours
Pump stations are always off during those hours
Groundwater levels peak at exactly the same time every night
optionA: Legitimate sanitary use is at its lowest then, so most of the remaining flow is infiltration
optionB: Rainfall never occurs during those hours
optionC: Pump stations are always off during those hours
optionD: Groundwater levels peak at exactly the same time every night
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: Two flow monitors in series on the same trunk sewer show the downstream monitor reading lower flow than the upstream monitor during dry weather. What should be checked first?
correctAnswer: Sensor installation, calibration and silt build up at the downstream site
explanation: Dry weather flow cannot normally decrease between two points in series without a diversion. Sensor fouling, poor installation or calibration drift at the downstream site is the first thing to verify.
options: Whether the downstream basin has been disconnected from the sewer
Sensor installation, calibration and silt build up at the downstream site
Whether rainfall gauges were read correctly that week
The colour coding used in the monitoring report
optionA: Whether the downstream basin has been disconnected from the sewer
optionB: Sensor installation, calibration and silt build up at the downstream site
optionC: Whether rainfall gauges were read correctly that week
optionD: The colour coding used in the monitoring report
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: A monitor record shows flow beginning to rise within minutes of rainfall starting and falling soon after rain stops. What source type does that timing point to?
correctAnswer: Direct inflow from surface or roof connections
explanation: A response that tracks rainfall almost immediately is direct inflow, such as roof leaders, cross connections or leaking covers. Groundwater infiltration responds much more slowly.
options: Slow groundwater infiltration through pipe joints
Tidal influence on the outfall
Leakage from a nearby watermain
Direct inflow from surface or roof connections
optionA: Slow groundwater infiltration through pipe joints
optionB: Tidal influence on the outfall
optionC: Leakage from a nearby watermain
optionD: Direct inflow from surface or roof connections
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.

question: In RDII analysis, what does the R value represent?
correctAnswer: The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration
explanation: The R value is the fraction of total rainfall volume over the tributary area that shows up in the sewer as RDII. It converts a rainfall volume into an RDII volume.
options: The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration
The roughness coefficient of the sewer pipe
The ratio of peak flow to average dry weather flow only
The percentage of the basin covered by rooftops
optionA: The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration
optionB: The roughness coefficient of the sewer pipe
optionC: The ratio of peak flow to average dry weather flow only
optionD: The percentage of the basin covered by rooftops
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rainfall Dependent I&I.

question: How does rainfall dependent I and I differ from groundwater infiltration in a flow record?
correctAnswer: RDII rises and falls in response to storm events, while groundwater infiltration is a slower, more sustained seasonal flow
explanation: RDII is storm driven and follows rainfall patterns over hours to days. Groundwater infiltration changes slowly with seasonal water table levels and forms a steadier base in the flow record.
options: RDII appears only in winter, while groundwater infiltration appears only in summer
RDII rises and falls in response to storm events, while groundwater infiltration is a slower, more sustained seasonal flow
RDII is clear water, while groundwater infiltration is always coloured
There is no practical difference in a flow record
optionA: RDII appears only in winter, while groundwater infiltration appears only in summer
optionB: RDII rises and falls in response to storm events, while groundwater infiltration is a slower, more sustained seasonal flow
optionC: RDII is clear water, while groundwater infiltration is always coloured
optionD: There is no practical difference in a flow record
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rainfall Dependent I&I.

question: After a long wet period, a basin hydrograph shows RDII peaks that keep growing with each successive storm, even for similar rainfall amounts. What does that trend suggest?
correctAnswer: Soils are becoming saturated, so a larger share of each storm enters the sewer
explanation: As soils saturate, less rain soaks away and more reaches defects and connections. Successive storms then produce larger RDII responses for the same rainfall.
options: The rain gauge is drifting out of calibration
Soils are becoming saturated, so a larger share of each storm enters the sewer
Residents are using less water during wet weather
The sewer is becoming less leaky over time
optionA: The rain gauge is drifting out of calibration
optionB: Soils are becoming saturated, so a larger share of each storm enters the sewer
optionC: Residents are using less water during wet weather
optionD: The sewer is becoming less leaky over time
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why is RDII normally compared between basins as a volume per unit area for a given storm, rather than as a raw peak flow?
correctAnswer: Normalizing by area allows a fair comparison between basins of different sizes
explanation: Basins differ in size, so raw flows are not comparable. RDII volume per hectare for the same storm puts every basin on the same basis for prioritization.
options: Raw peak flow is impossible to measure in a sewer
Normalizing by area allows a fair comparison between basins of different sizes
Volume per unit area is required for CCTV coding
Peak flow does not change during storms
optionA: Raw peak flow is impossible to measure in a sewer
optionB: Normalizing by area allows a fair comparison between basins of different sizes
optionC: Volume per unit area is required for CCTV coding
optionD: Peak flow does not change during storms
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Which investigation method is best suited to finding direct inflow sources such as roof leaders and cross connected drains in a high RDII basin?
correctAnswer: Smoke testing of the sanitary sewer
explanation: Smoke testing pressurizes the sanitary sewer with smoke that escapes at direct surface connections. It reveals roof leaders, area drains and cross connections that drive rapid inflow.
options: Smoke testing of the sanitary sewer
Pressure testing of the watermain network
Sludge depth sounding in the wet well
Acoustic leak detection on force mains
optionA: Smoke testing of the sanitary sewer
optionB: Pressure testing of the watermain network
optionC: Sludge depth sounding in the wet well
optionD: Acoustic leak detection on force mains

question: A monitored basin covers 25 ha. Dry weather analysis shows an excess inflow and infiltration flow of 8 L/s from the basin. What is the I and I rate per hectare? Round to 2 decimal places.
correctAnswer: 0.32 L/s/ha
explanation: I&I rate = Q / A. Substitute the stated values: 8 / 25 = 0.32 L/s/ha. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.
options: 3.13 L/s/ha
0.40 L/s/ha
0.25 L/s/ha
0.32 L/s/ha
optionA: 3.13 L/s/ha
optionB: 0.40 L/s/ha
optionC: 0.25 L/s/ha
optionD: 0.32 L/s/ha

question: A storm drops 25 mm of rain (0.025 m) over a 20000 m² catchment. The RDII coefficient R is 0.04. What volume of RDII enters the sewer? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: RDII volume = rainfall depth x area x R. Substitute the stated values: 0.025 x 20000 x 0.04 = 20.0 m³. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: Night flow monitoring in a 35 ha basin measures 18.5 L/s at the minimum hour. Legitimate night use is estimated at 4.5 L/s. What is the groundwater infiltration rate per hectare? Round to 2 decimal places.
correctAnswer: 0.40 L/s/ha
explanation: Infiltration rate = (measured night flow - legitimate use) / A. Substitute the stated values: (18.5 - 4.5) / 35 = 0.40 L/s/ha. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.
formula: Infiltration rate = (measured night flow - legitimate use) / A

0.66 L/s/ha

question: A 20 mm storm (0.02 m) falls on two subcatchments. Subcatchment A covers 10000 m² with R equal to 0.04, and subcatchment B covers 15000 m² with R equal to 0.06. What is the total RDII volume from both subcatchments? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: Total RDII = (depth x area A x R A) + (depth x area B x R B). Substitute the stated values: (0.02 x 10000 x 0.04) + (0.02 x 15000 x 0.06) = 26.0 m³. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.
formula: Total RDII = (depth x area A x R A) + (depth x area B x R B)

explanation: Percent complete = (completed north + completed south) / planned x 100. Substitute the stated values: (18500 + 14200) / 48000 x 100 = 68.1%. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.
formula: Percent complete = (completed north + completed south) / planned x 100
